brief.summary: Front-end and long-end yields are described as sharply higher, with the 2-year up over 50bp on the month and 30-year near 5.50%; the curve is seen steeper as term premia build. Friday brings modest stabilization, with front-end yields slightly lower and equity futures up about 0.1% after three days of gains. Oil is retreating, Brent near $93 down about 2%, on hopes for Iran/Strait talks, while the yen is firmer after intervention talk. The Fed is hawkish: officials flag further tightening and markets price roughly 3.5-4 hikes over the next year. The dominant narrative is higher-for-longer rates and a government-bond selloff, with credit spreads tight and AI capex optimism offset by financing concerns. Tone is cautious/neutral.
notable_quotes: This is a rate move on the government bond side, not necessarily on the corporate bond side.
Markets are no longer scared that tighter policy will ultimately derail growth.
